name: project_wac_ripul_strangler_auth
description: WAC↔Ripul strangler-fig + BYOA auth — how the SDK/CMS integrates into WAC where WAC owns auth
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 49c136d1-956b-4d96-88d9-e0131cc070ec
  scope: repo
  repo: wac-general
  scope_also: repo:ripul
---

Integrating the Ripul native CMS renderer into the **WAC iOS app** where **WAC owns auth**, riding the CMS strangler-fig proxy that is replacing WAC's Rails backend.

**State of the world (already built, discovered 2026-07-05):**
- RipulAgent SDK is **already a WAC dependency** (SPM `ripul-ios-sdk` v0.2.16; agent panel `WACAgentCoordinator` behind `RipulConfig.isAgentEnabled`, off by default).
- Strangler front-door is **live & app-selectable**: `ConfigurationHelper.cmsBaseUrl = "https://llm-proxy.ripul.io/v1/app/"` (catch-all → WAC).
- WAC already runs CMS-native queries but **site-key auth only** (no per-user identity): `JobPrefill.swift` → `POST /v1/cms-definitions/{id}/queries/{slug}/run` + `X-Site-Key` (`pk_live_qhzxe5zpbk2xb1v1lxb4z4sd`, origin `wac-ios.app`).
- **The WAC auth-provider + origin + routes are seeded/tested** in `chrome-extension/packages/payslip/scripts/cms-config.ts` targeting the live WAC CMS `cms_x5xpger1lv3j`. Enrich pipeline seeded DISABLED (ship-dark pattern). Verify which routes are actually enabled.

**WAC auth reality (why standard BYOA doesn't fit):**
- Token is **opaque BCrypt-hashed** in `authentication_tokens` (`secret` + `secret-id` custom headers, NOT Bearer, NOT a JWT). No JWKS → Rails must be the validation authority. Stored in iOS **UserDefaults** (not Keychain), non-refreshable, cleared on logout.
- Identity anchor = **phone/user-id**; **email deliberately never verified** (OTP plan). So Ripul's verified-email RLS join ([[project_byoa_rls_proxy_sso]], [[project_cms_directory_membership]]) is UNSAFE here.

**The design already keys correctly** — `auth_wac` provider: `credentialHeaders:['secret','secret-id']`, introspects `GET <wac>/api/v1/user`, `principalPath:'user.id'` → `principal.forcedUserId` → `bodyCtx.principalId` → RLS `WHERE user_id=@principalId` (handlers.ts:1657). RLS key = **WAC integer user.id, never email**. Cached 45s. Same WAC credential does double duty: proves identity to Ripul (introspection) AND passes through the proxy to Rails. Strangler switch = per-route `bind: proxy→WAC | query→native-SQL`, exact-match beats `/*` passthrough, additive per-table cutover, no app release. `withPrincipalHeader` injects `x-principal-id` downstream.

**The one real gap:** native `CmsClient` only speaks `Authorization: Bearer` (Clerk/site-key) and calls the DIRECT run endpoint (not an app-route), so it never triggers `auth_wac`. Close it via **Option A** (expose queries as `/v1/app/...` routes + `authProviderId:auth_wac`; teach CmsClient a credential mode sending secret/secret-id; load definition via site-key embedded-config not /admin) — MVP, reuses built machinery — or **Option B** (new Ripul endpoint mints short-lived session JWT `sub="wac:<user.id>"` from the WAC creds; renderer uses Bearer; Keychain-storable; clean end-state).

**SHIPPED 2026-07-14 (worker a4da7ad70 + admin UI 47ba79b53, deployed, migration 0036 applied):** opaque portalAuth + invite-only + blocked flag + @principalId binding + admin UI (block toggle, add-by-external-id, opaque settings) are LIVE. Gotcha fixed en route: no-Bearer-token requests 401'd BEFORE the BYOA fallbacks — opaque auth now hooks the missing-token gate in index.ts. NATIVE SHIPPED 2026-07-14: SDK v0.2.20 (monorepo cea42ac01, published via release-public.sh) — CmsClientConfig.portalCredentialProvider (opaque headers INSTEAD of Bearer), fetchPortalMembership, CmsPageLoader member mode + .noAccess state, CmsPage.requiredRoles + CmsPageVisibility (exact mirror of web pageVisibility.ts). WAC 77725db07 (feature/shift-rate-templates): RipulConfig.cmsId+portalCredentials() (preference.secret/secret_id), Testing-hub row "Ripul portal (member mode)" → DebugRipulPortalView. Validate from demo.ripul.io origin WORKS for the WAC key (embedded cms config present, 10 pages). CONFIG LIVE 2026-07-15: WAC key sk_3b7wtby33l2n ALREADY had live Clerk BYOA (clerk.wac.rocks) → shipped **portalAuthOpaque second slot** (81de26490; browser IdP + app creds coexist; opaque gate reads dedicated slot first; UI = switch section not third radio). D1-seeded: portalAuthOpaque {secret/secret-id → origin_wac /api/v1/user, user.id, subPrefix wac} + membershipPolicy invite-only (safe: no directoryTable, zero prior members). First member: wac:465097 (Peter, admin, email join peter.maude@gmail.com). Verified fail-closed: bogus/absent creds → 401; validate still returns clerk. Positive path tests from the WAC app (Testing hub → "Ripul portal (member mode)", needs OTA build installed).

**DECIDED 2026-07-14 (validated plan committed: `chrome-extension/docs/plans/wac-byoa-auth-integration.md`, d7b05d98d):** portal-*membership* path = new `portalAuth.provider:'opaque'` (id-first: `principalIdPath` required, sub=`wac:<user.id>`, email/display metadata only) + **invite-only `membershipPolicy`** (register/me fail closed — today register AUTO-ENROLLS any authed visitor and me JIT-binds from directoryTable, so delete ≠ block) + **`status:'blocked'` column on site_key_owners** (only revocation lever; WAC tokens never expire; 45s cache covers credential validation only, member lookup is live). Also: portal query runs DON'T bind `@principalId` today (only /v1/app/* does) — must bind raw WAC id when opaque-authed. Exactly 4 BYOA fallback points in packages/api/src/index.ts (register/run/design/me, ~1363/1384/1404/1416).

**GOTCHA hit 2026-07-15 — worker regression via parallel main deploy:** the BYOA work lived on ios-sdk/token-inspector; another session's deploy:all from main WIPED the opaque worker → app showed no-access despite perfect config (diagnosed by tailing llm-proxy with bogus creds: no [opaquePortalAuth] logs = old worker). RESOLVED: branch merged to main (2f3691d70) and main is THE working branch now. Second finding: WAC's edge (api3.workandcommunications.co.uk, Cloudflare WAF) 403s bot-like forwarded validation calls — CURL ALWAYS BLOCKED (don't debug with curl!), but the app's real forwarded headers PASS. **E2E PROVEN 2026-07-15: [opaquePortalAuth] authenticated wac:465097 (member: true) — WAC app renders the CMS portal as an invited member, no second login; block toggle verified live.** Diagnostics quieted to matched portal requests only.

**Validated Rails facts (2026-07-14):** `users.email` default `""` + `email_required?=false` + NON-unique → email join unusable (and a priv-esc vector, unverified); phone unique but nullable (social users). **Single-session tokens**: `create_token`→`destroy_old_tokens` destroys ALL tokens AND nils `fcm_id` (user.rb:896-926) → any portal phone+OTP login would log out the iOS app + kill push; browser phase blocked on WAC concurrent-token change. Headers: `secret` + `secret-id` (hyphen); `secret_id` only as param. In-app embedding (SDK passes existing token) sidesteps all of it — zero Rails changes.

**Safety musts:** `/api/v1/user` is the trust boundary (must be real Rails); RLS key=user.id never email; minimize WAC-secret blast radius (prefer B + Keychain); bound 45s revocation lag on logout; fail-closed (401 not silent 0-rows); gate renderer to iOS16+ (app floor is 13 — [[feedback_ios_deploy_device_first]]); writes keep WAC authoritative until cut over; ramp behind a flag.

Related: [[project_cms_transparent_proxy]], [[project_cms_native_renderer]], [[project_api_auth_scope_principal]], [[project_sitekey_mode_vs_token]], [[project_self_hosted_dev_loop_vision]].

**SIDEBAR MERGE 2026-07-15 (SDK v0.2.25, WAC OTA WAC-prod-202607151740):** CMS portal promoted out of debug hub into the REAL slide-out sidebar (RecordMenu, left-edge drawer — NOT the Profile hub). Protocol: SDK `CmsPortalMenuResolver.resolve(cmsId:siteKey:clientConfig:) -> CmsPortalMenu{isMember,role,canDesign,items[]}` contributes role-filtered nav (extracted from shell page's sidebarNav block, filtered via CmsPageVisibility like web filterTree), host renders. WAC: RipulPortalSidebar (cache+refresh+didUpdate), RipulPortalSidebarSection (native "Workplace" section, SF-symbol rows), inserted into RecordMenu scroll content below Status box (re-pins content bottom); gated on isMember; RecordMenuDelegate.didTapPortalPage → RecordsVC_MVVM opens CmsPageView at slug. GOTCHA: new Swift file must be registered in WAC.xcodeproj (checked-in pbxproj, NOT xcodegen) — added on disk only → "cannot find X in scope" compile fail; add PBXBuildFile+PBXFileReference+group+Sources entries (mirror RipulConfig.swift ids).

# Persistent derivedDataPath -> incremental builds. SAME per-flavour mapping as
# deploy-wac-ota.sh: prod shares /tmp/wac-device-dd (so device installs and prod OTA
# builds keep each other warm), every other flavour gets its own path — otherwise a
# beta device install would fight the prod build.db lock, and would build beta into a
# different dd than the beta OTA path, wasting the incremental state twice over.
case "$FLAVOR" in prod) DD="/tmp/wac-device-dd";; *) DD="/tmp/wac-dd-$FLAVOR";; esac

# WAC_LIVE_CONTROL=1 -> a developer build for Ripul Live View. The SDK compiles real
# touches and its fast screen capture into Debug builds only (they use private API),
# and our flavours are Release configs, so a normal install can be SEEN in Live View
# but not touched. This sets the SDK's RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD condition instead of
# switching to Debug (which would mean the dev backend). Same xcconfig, same backend.
# Direct installs to our own phones ONLY: the OTA and TestFlight scripts never set it,
# and it builds into its own derivedDataPath so nothing compiled this way can be
# picked up by a build that ships.
LIVE_FLAGS=()
if [ "${WAC_LIVE_CONTROL:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  DD="$DD-live"
  LIVE_FLAGS=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD')
fi
# A non-default Xcode (e.g. DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app/Contents/Developer
# to try the iOS 27 SDK) gets its own derivedDataPath: two toolchains in one dd force full
# rebuilds and can leave stale precompiled modules for the next default-Xcode build.
# (xcode-select -p itself honours DEVELOPER_DIR, so ask it with the variable unset.)
if [ -n "${DEVELOPER_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$DEVELOPER_DIR" != "$(env -u DEVELOPER_DIR xcode-select -p)" ]; then
  DD="$DD-$(basename "${DEVELOPER_DIR%%.app/*}")"
fi
TEAM="C7AA358R56"
FAST="${FAST:-1}"            # 1 = fast dev-loop build; 0 = fully optimized Release. Set FAST=0 to opt out.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$REPO_ROOT"
# Signing without an Xcode account: the App Store Connect key, when this Mac has one.
. "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/asc-key.sh"
B="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)"
LOG="/tmp/wac-device-build-$B.log"

# Release config (needed for Production.xcconfig -> prod backend) defaults to
# SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE=wholemodule + -O, which recompiles ALL ~1200 Swift files
# on ANY 1-line change (minutes). These overrides keep -configuration Release (prod
# backend + #if DEBUG still false) but switch the COMPILE to true-incremental, no-opt,
# and skip the dSYM bundle + index store -> a 1-line change rebuilds in seconds.
# Doesn't change which xcconfig/backend is used. Set FAST=0 for a real optimized Release.

---
name: Embedded agent identity foundation
description: "20 Oct 2026: empty employment controls hidden, retaining former-job history; live iPhone review verified with names, transcript and minimize/restore. Manager reply and corrections remain."
metadata:
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  type: project
---

The plan is Ripul artefact `art_1c584739-140d-4f8c-9a6f-aba99de0ede8`, revision 37.
Peter explicitly chose artefacts instead of the retiring planning tools.

**Decisions:** one immutable EMP code/stable employment per conversation. One WAC
account can hold several separate job identities. Codes are claimed exclusively;
manager unlocking increments generation and gives no old-history transfer, even
to the same account. Leaving employment instead preserves original-participant
conversation access, without restoring live employer-data permissions. One manager
per company; immediate escalation. Company managers choose one-click manager approval
(default) or opt-in employee-approved automation. Corrections cover wac in/out and
breaks only. The app edits shifts, existing pipeline confirms; no direct downstream
patches. Cloudflare runners, existing WAC notifications and CMS reminder intervals.
Retention deferred. Existing AI Helper stream/composer/navigation is the required UI.

**Deployed:** migration 0093, dedicated embedded-agent API, CMS schema mappings and
company allowlist. WAC site cms_x5xpger1lv3j allows company WAC only. Mapping employees:
unique_code / employee_code / company_id / status, active/in-active. Opaque WAC login
is verified server-side; 15-minute hashed sessions. Claims are atomic; conversation
bindings have a database immutability trigger. Public and internal site-key forms
resolve the same customer. Availability is non-claiming. Server stamps authors.
First actual beta “Hi” was verified live on 19 Oct at 18:11 BST with current claim
and generation. No further live messages were generated by the UI test.

**Shared Helper:** Ripul main cb59715b6 deployed by web train 2768. SDK 0.7.178
public commit 546048580767a3c8daa8110b192e61278d254fdf. WAC integration lives in its
own repo/worktree WAC_ios_final-embedded-agents, feature/embedded-agent-reconciliation;
beta 2.6.5/202610191919 on https://wac-ota.osintsupport.workers.dev/install.html.
Its memory contains the WAC-specific implementation and runtime-audit inventory.
Native advertises embeddedAgent; NativeBridge connects embeddedChatStore and
externalChatTabs to the same ChatView/native composer. No customer secrets enter JS.
Employment history/titles are not persisted to personal/anonymous caches, and native
MessageHistory excludes ecv_ messages. Account epoch changes and access denial clear
employment state. Ordinary session mutation/runner paths refuse employment threads.

**Validation:** 136 relevant web unit checks, shared web type check, Swift client
harness and MessageHistory check, WAC compile and four convention lints pass. Clean
WebKit on deployed shared UI with a deterministic native transport exercised saved
Hi, native send, two jobs, reopen/reload, sessions and reset. This is a fixture test,
not evidence of new real-device authentication. Phone reopening/multi-job switching
and full View Explorer/theme/text audits remain unverified (WAC phone unavailable).

**Next:** verify the real dashboard-to-phone manager reply; finish the phone layout
audit. The nominated manager is configured and Join permission verified. Unlock API/UI (internal primitive
exists), approval/reminder controls, notifications, shift edit/pipeline integration,
attachments, employee >200-message pagination and further CMS adapters remain.
Manager history pagination is implemented. The full correction workflow is not
complete. Contract/tests: chrome-extension/docs/features/embeddedAgentIdentity.md.

**Cloud discussion pilot, 20 October:** commit `656eb0408`, web train 2895,
worker version `bebe6929-0aa9-4b08-bef1-05d334b1eff9`, Pages build `mvgqu6kw`.
Migration 0097 adds issue snapshots and turn state. `EmbeddedAgentRunner` is a
SQLite Durable Object per conversation, with persistent ordered tasks and alarms,
four-attempt retries and deterministic agent message IDs. Existing AI Gateway
Anthropic route runs Haiku; no shift tools, manager invitations or approvals.
CMS `embeddedAgents.runner = {enabled:true, allowedBindingKeys:[...]}` separately
opts in employment codes. WAC currently opts in only Peter's `WAC-Q095BM2J`;
company allowlist remains WAC. Unlinked ordinary threads remain storage-only.

Operator POST `/admin/cms-definitions/:cmsId/embedded-agent-issues` requires CMS
administration, CMS boundary checks and no view-as. It accepts an already claimed
employment, immutable issue key and source facts. No `/v1` prefix on CMS admin
routes. Reads/replies recheck claim generation, mapping, current binding/company,
provider fingerprint, site and account block. Claim recovery loses the old thread;
former employment retains participation.

Live issue `shift:14653247:rota:file_38b096f0b2a4c74fb6816d98:v2` created conversation
`ecv_7b41b12c-c363-43fb-b9f1-16dfe70336cd`, site `sk_3b7wtby33l2n`, claim generation 1.
The first real cloud reply completed on attempt 1 at 14:56 BST: 15 October rota
09:00–17:00 versus actual 09:30–17:00, both 30-minute unpaid break; asks what
happened. It initially awaited the employee; later replies are verified below.
Earlier Hi remains in its original thread. No synthetic
employee response was submitted. Fresh BigQuery read reconfirmed both test shifts.

Shared Helper polls active/visible messages every three seconds. Older WAC beta
strips the explicit role but preserves IDs; server-reserved `eam_` IDs render as
assistant messages, and employee writes cannot use that prefix. Existing beta
202610201353 needs no install: reopen Helper/load latest shared web. Job shortcut
or Refresh jobs + choose Wac opens its newest thread.

Validation: 36 backend tests (including real Miniflare DO persistence across
restart, ordering, bounded retries), 10 web tests, web typecheck and deployed
     213 chrome-extension/docs/features/embeddedAgentIdentity.md

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Refuses a store build that carries private Apple functions.

  check_private_apis.py source                  the code that goes into store builds
  check_private_apis.py binary <app|ipa|xcarchive>   a built app
  check_private_apis.py all <app|ipa|xcarchive>      both

  --allow-known   let through what private-apis.json lists as "known" (tester
                  builds only; never a build meant for App Store review)

Exit 0 when clean, 1 when something was found, 2 on a usage error.

Two checks, because each misses what the other finds:

  source  Every line that reaches for something by name at runtime (dlsym,
          NSSelectorFromString, NSClassFromString, underscore keys, runtime
          class surgery) must be compiled out of store builds by
          `#if DEBUG` / `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`, or be listed in
          private-apis.json. A line that is neither is NEW and fails, whatever
          the flags: it has to be gated or reviewed first.

  binary  The names themselves, looked for in what is about to ship. This is
          the proof that a developer switch did not leak into the build.
          Short names (15 bytes or fewer) can be folded into code by the
          optimiser and escape it, which is why the source check exists.

This catches the usual ways of reaching private functions. It is not proof
that there are none. See ripul-native-app/docs/app-store-private-apis.md.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
REGISTER = os.path.join(HERE, "private-apis.json")

LOOKUP = re.compile(
    r"dlsym\(|dlopen\(|NSSelectorFromString\(|NSClassFromString\(|Selector\(\(|@_silgen_name|@objc\(_"
    r"|objc_getClass|objc_allocateClassPair|object_setClass|class_getInstanceMethod|class_getInstanceVariable"
    r"|method_exchangeImplementations|class_addMethod|class_replaceMethod|method_setImplementation"
    r"|MGCopyAnswer|LSApplicationWorkspace|PrivateFrameworks"
    r"|forKey: \"_|forKeyPath: \"_|value\(forKey: \"[a-z]|setValue\([^\n]*forKey: \"[a-z_]"
)
# KVC on our own requests and defaults is everywhere and is not a lookup of Apple's code.
NOT_A_LOOKUP = re.compile(r"forHTTPHeaderField|UserDefaults|\.standard\.|defaults\.|setValue\([^\n]*forKey: \"[a-z][A-Za-z]*\"\)\s*//\s*public")
DEVELOPER_ONLY = re.compile(r"\bDEBUG\b|\bRIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD\b")
NOT_IOS = re.compile(r"^NOT\(os\(iOS\)\)$|^os\(macOS\)$|^canImport\(AppKit\) && !targetEnvironment\(macCatalyst\)$")


def load_register():
    with open(REGISTER) as handle:
        return json.load(handle)


def gates(lines, index):
55:def load_register():
60:def gates(lines, index):
76:def check_source(register, allow_known):
84:            sys.exit(2)
137:def executables(app):
155:def find_app(target, scratch):
169:def check_binary(register, target, allow_known):
174:            sys.exit(2)
204:def main():
205:    arguments = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
206:    allow_known = "--allow-known" in sys.argv
210:        sys.exit(2)
220:        sys.exit(1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The binary check refuses an app that carries a developer-only name, the SDK's site switch included."""
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
import io
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile

import check_private_apis as checker

MACH_O = b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe"


class BinaryCheckTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.register = checker.load_register()

    def app(self, *strings, name="WAC"):
        app = os.path.join(self.temp.name, f"{name}.app")
        os.makedirs(app, exist_ok=True)
        body = MACH_O + b"\0" * 64 + b"\0".join(s.encode() for s in ("_TtC11RipulAgent10AgentBridge", *strings)) + b"\0"
        with open(os.path.join(app, name), "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(body)
        return app

    def check(self, target, allow_known=False):
        out = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out):
            failed = checker.check_binary(self.register, target, allow_known)
        return failed, out.getvalue()

    def test_store_build_without_the_switch_is_clean(self):
        failed, out = self.check(self.app())
        self.assertFalse(failed, out)
        self.assertIn("none of the registered names", out)

    def test_site_switch_marker_stops_the_upload(self):
        failed, out = self.check(self.app("RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN"))
        self.assertTrue(failed)
        self.assertIn("developer-tools-site-switch", out)
        self.assertIn("RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS", out)

    def test_allow_known_does_not_let_the_switch_through(self):
        failed, _ = self.check(self.app("RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN"), allow_known=True)
        self.assertTrue(failed)

    def test_marker_inside_an_ipa_is_found(self):
        app = self.app("RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN")
        ipa = os.path.join(self.temp.name, "WAC.ipa")
        with zipfile.ZipFile(ipa, "w") as archive:
            for folder, _, files in os.walk(app):
                for file in files:
                    path = os.path.join(folder, file)
                    archive.write(path, os.path.join("Payload", os.path.relpath(path, self.temp.name)))
        failed, out = self.check(ipa)

content.content:
## Which builds may carry developer-only code

| Build | Made by | Configuration | Developer-only code | May go to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Device and OTA development builds | `ship-ios.sh`, `ship-ota.sh`, `ship_ios.py` | Debug | **Yes** | Your own registered devices |
| Simulator | `ship_duo_sim.py` | Debug | **Yes** | Simulators |
| Mac host, Catalyst | `build_mac.py`, the Catalyst command | Debug | **Yes** | Your own Mac |
| **TestFlight and App Store** | `deploy-testflight.sh` | **Release** | **No. Checked before upload** | Testers, App Store review |
| A host app's developer build (WAC) | `WAC_LIVE_CONTROL=1 install-wac-device.sh` | Release + `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` | **Yes** | Your own devices, installed directly |
| A host app's OTA, TestFlight and store builds | its own deploy scripts | Release | **No** | Anyone |
| The device runner | `device-runner/run.sh` | Debug, a UI-test bundle | **Yes, all of it** | Your own registered devices and simulators. It is a separate app and is never submitted |

The device runner (`ripul-native-app/device-runner`) is a UI-test runner that controls a whole phone through Apple's test daemon, as Appium's does. It calls XCTest's own unpublished classes and is a developer tool by nature: it is no part of Ripul or the SDK, has its own bundle id, and `check_private_apis.py` does not scan its folder. Nothing from that folder may be compiled into an app target.

A support session (`RipulSupport` in the SDK, [support-sessions.md](../../ripul-ios-sdk/docs/support-sessions.md)) is the part of Live View that does ship: a customer shows the app to a supporter, who can point but not touch. It uses none of the above. The picture is the app's own drawing of its window (`drawHierarchy`), nothing is injected into the app, and the support mode never takes the render-server capture or the synthesized touches even in a build that has them.

## The two switches

| Switch | Set by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEBUG` | Xcode, in a Debug configuration | A development build |
| `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` | The command line of a direct install, for a host app whose test builds are Release builds | The same, for that one build. Passed as `'SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD'` |

Neither is ever set in a project file, an xcconfig or a scheme. If one were, every build would inherit it.

  -workspace WAC.xcworkspace -scheme "$SCHEME" -configuration "$CONFIG" \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath "$DD" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates ${ASC_AUTH[@]+"${ASC_AUTH[@]}"} CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM" \
  "${FAST_FLAGS[@]+"${FAST_FLAGS[@]}"}" \
  "${LIVE_FLAGS[@]+"${LIVE_FLAGS[@]}"}" \
  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$B" > "$LOG" 2>&1 \
  || { echo "BUILD FAILED — tail $LOG:"; tail -25 "$LOG"; exit 1; }

APP="$DD/Build/Products/$CONFIG-iphoneos/WAC.app"
[ -d "$APP" ] || { echo "error: no app at $APP"; exit 1; }
DD="/tmp/wac-sim-dd-$FLAVOR"

# WAC_LIVE_CONTROL=1 -> a build Ripul Live View can drive, not only see. Same switch,
# same reasons as install-wac-device.sh: it sets the SDK's RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD
# condition, keeps the flavour's config and backend, and builds into its own dd.
LIVE_FLAGS=()
if [ "${WAC_LIVE_CONTROL:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  DD="$DD-live"
  LIVE_FLAGS=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD')
fi
FAST="${FAST:-1}"            # 1 = fast dev-loop build; 0 = fully optimized Release.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$REPO_ROOT"
B="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)"
LOG="/tmp/wac-sim-build-$B.log"

# Keep -configuration Release (prod backend, #if DEBUG still false) but switch the
# COMPILE to true-incremental/no-opt so a 1-line change rebuilds in seconds. See the
# same block in install-wac-device.sh.
FAST_FLAGS=()
if [ "$FAST" = "1" ]; then
  FAST_FLAGS=(
    SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE=incremental
    SWIFT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=-Onone
    GCC_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=0
    DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT=dwarf
    COMPILER_INDEX_STORE_ENABLE=NO
    ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO
  )
fi

echo "==> build $FLAVOR: $SCHEME/$CONFIG #$B for simulator $SIM (FAST=$FAST, live control=${WAC_LIVE_CONTROL:-0}, incremental via $DD)  log: $LOG"
caffeinate -ims xcodebuild build \
  -workspace WAC.xcworkspace -scheme "$SCHEME" -configuration "$CONFIG" \
  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIM" -derivedDataPath "$DD" \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  "${FAST_FLAGS[@]+"${FAST_FLAGS[@]}"}" \
  "${LIVE_FLAGS[@]+"${LIVE_FLAGS[@]}"}" \
  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$B" > "$LOG" 2>&1 \
  || { echo "BUILD FAILED — tail $LOG:"; tail -25 "$LOG"; exit 1; }

input.command:
cd /tmp/wac-site-key-switch && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
for p in ['scripts/install-wac-device.sh','scripts/install-wac-simulator.sh']:
    s=open(p).read()
    old="""  LIVE_FLAGS=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD')
fi"""
    new="""  LIVE_FLAGS=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD')
elif [ "$FLAVOR" != "prod" ]; then
  # Dev, staging and beta get the SDK's developer levers that use no private API:
  # RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS, which compiles in the dev helper's "Ripul Site" switch
  # (RipulSiteSwitch). Prod keeps only the compiled site key. Never on TestFlight:
  # deploy-testflight.sh refuses an app carrying the switch.
  LIVE_FLAGS=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS')
fi"""
    assert old in s, p
    s=s.replace(old,new)
    open(p,'w').write(s)

p='scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh'
s=open(p).read()
old="""  scheme="$(flavor_scheme "$flavor")"; config="$(flavor_config "$flavor")"; title="$(flavor_title "$flavor")"
"""
new="""  scheme="$(flavor_scheme "$flavor")"; config="$(flavor_config "$flavor")"; title="$(flavor_title "$flavor")"
  # Sideloaded dev, staging and beta builds get the SDK's developer levers that use
  # no private API (RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS: the dev helper's "Ripul Site" switch).
  # Prod keeps only its compiled site key. TestFlight never gets it.
  local devtools=()
  [ "$flavor" != "prod" ] && devtools=('SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=$(inherited) RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS')
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="""        ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO \\
        > "$stage/archive.log" 2>&1"""
new="""        ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO "${devtools[@]+"${devtools[@]}"}" \\
        > "$stage/archive.log" 2>&1"""
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="""      CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM" CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$B" \\
      > "$stage/archive.log" 2>&1 || die "archive failed — see $stage/archive.log\""""
new="""      CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM" CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$B" "${devtools[@]+"${devtools[@]}"}" \\
      > "$stage/archive.log" 2>&1 || die "archive failed — see $stage/archive.log\""""
assert s.count(old)==1, 'archive'; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
bash -n scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh scripts/install-wac-device.sh scripts/install-wac-simulator.sh && echo syntax-ok; grep -n "local scheme config" scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh

content.content:
if [ -n "$k_id" ] && [ -n "$k_issuer" ] && [ -f "$k_path" ]; then
    # altool finds AuthKey_<id>.p8 in API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR.
    export API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR="$(dirname "$k_path")"
    ALTOOL_AUTH=(--apiKey "$k_id" --apiIssuer "$k_issuer")
  fi
fi

upload_ipa() {
  local ipa="$1"
  [ -f "$ipa" ] || die "IPA not found: $ipa"
  echo "==> validating with App Store Connect (altool --validate-app, auth: ${ALTOOL_AUTH[0]})"
  if ! xcrun altool --validate-app -f "$ipa" -t ios \
        "${ALTOOL_AUTH[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$STAGE/validate.log"; then
    die "validation failed — see $STAGE/validate.log"
  fi
  echo "==> uploading to TestFlight (altool --upload-app)"
  if ! xcrun altool --upload-app -f "$ipa" -t ios \
        "${ALTOOL_AUTH[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$STAGE/upload.log"; then
    die "upload failed — see $STAGE/upload.log"
    die "archive failed — full log: $STAGE/archive.log"
  fi
  [ -d "$ARCHIVE" ] || die "archive step exited 0 but produced no .xcarchive — see $STAGE/archive.log"

input.content:
# Switching the Ripul site from the SDK's dev helper

Branch `sdk-site-key-switch` in ripul and in the wac iPhone repo, 21 October 2026, written during the freeze for George's client demo. Nothing here is deployed, installed or applied to a live site.

## What it is for

George demos the WAC business portal on Demo Company, a site with invented data (`wac-demo-wrap`, `cms_8fmfr6zq7mhn`, key `sk_479undka5gp4`). The to-do list's AI Conversation, where the manager resolves a shift with the employee on their phone, works only on the real portal (`wac`, `cms_x5xpger1lv3j`), because only the real portal's site key has the wac app's sign-in and the embedded-agents mapping.

The goal is a sideloaded dev or beta wac build, pointed at the demo site from the SDK's dev helper, so a phone can hold a real conversation against demo data. The lever is generic: any app on the SDK gets it.

## Peter's model

- **Prod and TestFlight builds:** the app uses the site key compiled into it, and the binary has no switching code.
- **Dev and sideloaded beta builds:** the compiled key is still the default. The dev helper can put another site's key in its place, and the portal, the agent and conversations all follow. Reset goes back to the compiled key, and signing out clears the choice. A marker shows while the app is pointed at another site.
- **The server is the backstop.** The dropdown lists only sites the signed-in Ripul person belongs to. Each site's key, membership and row rules still decide what comes back.
- **Only Ripul moves.** The wac app's shifts, wac in/out and login still come from WAC's Rails backend and Firestore.

## Findings

### The dev helper

The dev helper is the SDK's `RipulDevAssistantOverlay` (`Sessions/RipulDevAssistantOverlay.swift`): a floating bubble that opens `RipulAgentConsole`. The console has its own Ripul (Clerk) sign-in, the machines and sessions list, Solutions, Profile and Console Logs. Its levers are the overflow menu (`Sessions/SessionListMenu.swift`) and the tools it registers (`DevToolsModifier`: inspection, touches, explorer).

In wac, `RipulDevConsoleConfig` (`DebugTestingHubVC.swift`) configures it with an isolated cache suite `com.wac.ripuldev` and its own web data store. `AppDelegate` installs the restore hook, and Profile opens it. All of this is inside `#if WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.

**How it is compiled in and out today:**

- **In the SDK:** it is not. The SDK compiles the overlay and console into every build. Only private functions are compiled out, under `DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`.
- **In wac:** only the entry points are compiled out, by `WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.

### Which wac configurations are which

| Configuration | Scheme | Conditions | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Release` | WAC (prod) | `KDCALENDAR_EVENT_MANAGER_ENABLED WAC_APPLE_SIGN_IN` | App Store, TestFlight, prod OTA |
| `Release(Beta)` | WAC(Beta) | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` | Beta OTA, device installs |
| `Release(Dev)` | WAC(Dev) | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS WAC_APPLE_SIGN_IN` | Dev OTA |
| `Release(Staging)`, `Release(Business)` | | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` | |
| `Debug*` | | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` (and `-D DEBUG` on most) | Xcode runs |

Beta is a Release configuration, so `DEBUG` cannot mark it, and an app target's conditions do not reach a Swift package. Only the xcodebuild command line reaches the SDK. That is how wac already passes `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` for Live View (`WAC_LIVE_CONTROL=1 install-wac-device.sh`).

### Does TestFlight strip the dev helper?

**wac's own pieces are stripped:**

- `deploy-testflight.sh` refuses any configuration that defines `WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.
- So only prod `Release` can be uploaded today. Beta and dev TestFlight uploads are refused outright.

**The SDK's code is not stripped (measured 21 Oct):** in a `Release` (prod) WAC build for the simulator, made from `v3` at `882ff569d` against SDK 0.7.169:

- **Gone:** `RipulDevConsoleConfig` and `com.wac.ripuldev`, wac's own.

## What it is for

George demos the WAC business portal on Demo Company, a site with invented data (`wac-demo-wrap`, `cms_8fmfr6zq7mhn`, key `sk_479undka5gp4`). The to-do list's AI Conversation, where the manager resolves a shift with the employee on their phone, works only on the real portal (`wac`, `cms_x5xpger1lv3j`), because only the real portal's site key has the wac app's sign-in and the embedded-agents mapping.

The goal is a sideloaded dev or beta wac build, pointed at the demo site from the SDK's dev helper, so a phone can hold a real conversation against demo data. The lever is generic: any app on the SDK gets it.

## Peter's model

- **Prod and TestFlight builds:** the app uses the site key compiled into it, and the binary has no switching code.
- **Dev and sideloaded beta builds:** the compiled key is still the default. The dev helper can put another site's key in its place, and the portal, the agent and conversations all follow. - **The server is the backstop.** The dropdown lists only sites the signed-in Ripul person belongs to. Each site's key, membership and row rules still decide what comes back.

# Switching the Ripul site from the SDK's dev helper

Branch `sdk-site-key-switch` in ripul and in the wac iPhone repo, 21 October 2026, written during the freeze for George's client demo. Nothing here is deployed, installed or applied to a live site.

## What it is for

George demos the WAC business portal on Demo Company, a site with invented data (`wac-demo-wrap`, `cms_8fmfr6zq7mhn`, key `sk_479undka5gp4`). The to-do list's AI Conversation, where the manager resolves a shift with the employee on their phone, works only on the real portal (`wac`, `cms_x5xpger1lv3j`), because only the real portal's site key has the wac app's sign-in and the embedded-agents mapping.

The goal is a sideloaded dev or beta wac build, pointed at the demo site from the SDK's dev helper, so a phone can hold a real conversation against demo data. The lever is generic: any app on the SDK gets it.

## Peter's model

- **Prod and TestFlight builds:** the app uses the site key compiled into it, and the binary has no switching code.
- **Dev and sideloaded beta builds:** the compiled key is still the default. The dev helper can put another site's key in its place, and the portal, the agent and conversations all follow. Reset goes back to the compiled key, and signing out clears the choice. A marker shows while the app is pointed at another site.
- **The server is the backstop.** The dropdown lists only sites the signed-in Ripul person belongs to. Each site's key, membership and row rules still decide what comes back.
- **Only Ripul moves.** The wac app's shifts, wac in/out and login still come from WAC's Rails backend and Firestore.

## Findings

### The dev helper

The dev helper is the SDK's `RipulDevAssistantOverlay` (`Sessions/RipulDevAssistantOverlay.swift`): a floating bubble that opens `RipulAgentConsole`. The console has its own Ripul (Clerk) sign-in, the machines and sessions list, Solutions, Profile and Console Logs. Its levers are the overflow menu (`Sessions/SessionListMenu.swift`) and the tools it registers (`DevToolsModifier`: inspection, touches, explorer).

In wac, `RipulDevConsoleConfig` (`DebugTestingHubVC.swift`) configures it with an isolated cache suite `com.wac.ripuldev` and its own web data store. `AppDelegate` installs the restore hook, and Profile opens it. All of this is inside `#if WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.

**How it is compiled in and out today:**

- **In the SDK:** it is not. The SDK compiles the overlay and console into every build. Only private functions are compiled out, under `DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`.
- **In wac:** only the entry points are compiled out, by `WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.

### Which wac configurations are which

| Configuration | Scheme | Conditions | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Release` | WAC (prod) | `KDCALENDAR_EVENT_MANAGER_ENABLED WAC_APPLE_SIGN_IN` | App Store, TestFlight, prod OTA |
| `Release(Beta)` | WAC(Beta) | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` | Beta OTA, device installs |
| `Release(Dev)` | WAC(Dev) | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS WAC_APPLE_SIGN_IN` | Dev OTA |
| `Release(Staging)`, `Release(Business)` | | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` | |
| `Debug*` | | `… WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` (and `-D DEBUG` on most) | Xcode runs |

Beta is a Release configuration, so `DEBUG` cannot mark it, and an app target's conditions do not reach a Swift package. Only the xcodebuild command line reaches the SDK. That is how wac already passes `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` for Live View (`WAC_LIVE_CONTROL=1 install-wac-device.sh`).

### Does TestFlight strip the dev helper?

**wac's own pieces are stripped:**

- `deploy-testflight.sh` refuses any configuration that defines `WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.
- So only prod `Release` can be uploaded today. Beta and dev TestFlight uploads are refused outright.

**The SDK's code is not stripped (measured 21 Oct):** in a `Release` (prod) WAC build for the simulator, made from `v3` at `882ff569d` against SDK 0.7.169:

- **Gone:** `RipulDevConsoleConfig` and `com.wac.ripuldev`, wac's own.
- **Still in the binary:** `RipulDevAssistantOverlay` (3 symbols), `RipulDevOverlayWindow` (6), `ConsoleLogViewer` (338), `DevToolsModifier` (52) and the `RipulAgentConsole` type strings.

The helper is unreachable in prod, but it is present. Compiling it out of the SDK is a separate change, listed under follow-ups. The new switch does not have this problem.

### How wac hands its site to the SDK

- **Where it lives:** `WAC/Agent/RipulConfig.swift` holds `siteKey = "pk_live_qhzxe5zpbk2xb1v1lxb4z4sd"` (site `sk_3b7wtby33l2n`), `cmsId = "cms_x5xpger1lv3j"` and `originHeader = "https://wac-ios.app"`.
- **What reads it:** every Ripul surface reads those constants: the portal sidebar and pages, the agent coordinator, `JobPrefill`, `RipulEventClient`, the support session and the debug portal. On `feature/embedded-agent-reconciliation`, `WACEmploymentConversations` passes `RipulConfig.siteKey` to `EmbeddedAgentClient` too.
- **The repo:** the live branch is `v3`, checked out at `~/Documents/WAC_ios_final-shift-rate-templates`. wac pins the SDK from `github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk` at an exact version (0.7.169).

### The server call

Nothing listed the sites a person belongs to:

- `/admin/site-keys` needs `admin:manage_site_keys`.
- `/v1/artefacts/sites` lists owner and admin sites only, plus every site for a global admin.

So this branch adds one.

## The design built on these branches

### Compile condition: `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`

The switch is compiled in under `DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`. The new `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` means "developer levers that use no private function".

**Why a new condition:**

- **`DEBUG` misses beta.** Beta is a Release configuration.
- **`RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD` brings too much.** It carries Live View's private touch and capture code, which a beta OTA for George should not need.
- **An SPM trait cannot vary by configuration.**
- **A runtime flag would leave the code in prod.**

**How a build gets it:** it is passed on the command line, like `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`, by the wac scripts for dev, staging and beta only. It is never set in a project file, an xcconfig or a scheme.

**What a store build keeps:** only a pass-through API. `RipulSiteSwitch.siteKey(compiled:)` and `cmsId(compiled:compiledKey:)` return what they are given, `register` and `reset` do nothing, and `isAvailable` is false.

**Measured** (SDK objects, iOS simulator):

| Build | `RipulSiteSwitch.o` | Marker string | Endpoint string |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Release | 50 KB | absent | absent |
| Release with `-DRIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` | 212 KB | present | present |
| Debug | | present | present |

### SDK (`ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/SiteSwitch/`)

- **The API (`RipulSiteSwitch`):**
  - `register(CompiledSite)` is called once at launch with the key, the definition, the origin and a name.
  - `siteKey(compiled:)` and `cmsId(compiled:compiledKey:)` return the site to use.
  - `reset()` goes back to the compiled site.
  - `didChange` is posted when the choice changes.
  - `marker` is `"RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN"`.
- **The stored choice:**
  - It is kept in `UserDefaults` under `io.ripul.siteSwitch.choice.v1`.
  - It is tied to the compiled key it was made over, so a build that compiles in another key ignores it.
  - Picking the compiled site clears it.
- **The lever:** the console's menu gets a "Ripul Site…" row, for the developer audience and only once the app has registered. It opens `RipulSiteSwitchScreen` (`.ripulSheet`, theme tokens only), which shows:
  - the Default, which is the compiled site;
  - "Your sites", from the endpoint below, filtered to keys that accept the app's origin;
  - a checkmark on the site in use, and Reset;
  - a note that screens already open keep their site until reopened.
- **The marker:** a pill at the top of every scene ("Ripul site: wac Demo"), in its own pass-through `RipulChromeWindow`. Tapping it offers Reset. It is drawn again on `UIScene.didActivate`.
- **Sign-out:** `RipulClerkAuthStore.signOut()` (the dev helper's Ripul account) resets the choice. The app resets it on its own sign-out too.
- **Tests:** `Tests/RipulAgentTests/RipulSiteSwitchTests.swift`, 7 tests.

### Server: `GET /v1/site-key/memberships?origin=…`

`siteKeys/handlers.ts` `handleSiteKeyMemberships`.

**Who may call it:**

- **Only a person's own Ripul sign-in** (`authSource === 'clerk_jwt'` with a user id). A site key or machine token gets a 403.
- **Rows matched by user id only.** No email match, because a tenant's IdP could assert any email, and listing by email would show which other sites that email belongs to.

**What it lists:**

- Active `site_key_owners` rows on enabled keys, sorted by name.
- With `origin`, only keys whose `allowedOrigins` accept it.

**What it returns:** for each site, `siteKeyId`, `publishableKey`, `name`, `slug`, `cmsDefinitionId` (resolving `delegateCmsDefinitionTo`) and `role`. Responses are `no-store`.

It is a menu, not a grant: every request to a chosen site goes through that site's own checks. Tests: `siteKeys/__tests__/siteKeyMemberships.test.ts`, 5 tests.

### Upload checks

- **Ripul:** `check_private_apis.py` lists `RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN` as a `never` name. `deploy-testflight.sh` already runs `all` on the app, so an app carrying the switch is refused, and `--allow-known` does not let it through. Tests: `scripts/test_check_private_apis.py`, 6 tests.
- **wac: the settings gate.** `deploy-testflight.sh` now also refuses a configuration that defines `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` or `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`.
- **wac: the binary check.** The new `scripts/check_store_build.py` reads the IPA before validation, in upload-only mode too.
  - **Refused:** the switch marker, and wac's `RipulDevConsoleConfig` and `com.wac.ripuldev`.
  - **Reported but not refused:** the SDK's own dev-helper types, which every build carries today. `WAC_STRICT_DEV_HELPER=1` refuses them once the SDK compiles them out.
  - **Tests:** `scripts/test_check_store_build.py`, 6 tests.
  - **On real builds:** the prod probe passes, with the three SDK notes. The current beta build fails on wac's dev-helper config, as it should.

### wac (`sdk-site-key-switch`, from `v3`)

- **Reading the site:**
  - `RipulConfig.compiledSiteKey` and `compiledCmsId` are the compiled values.
  - `siteKey` and `cmsId` become computed through `RipulSiteSwitch`.
  - `registerCompiledSite()` runs at the top of `didFinishLaunching`.
  - `resetSite()` runs in `PreferenceHelper.logOut()`.
- **The sidebar:** `RipulPortalSidebar` drops its cached menu and resolves again on `didChange`.
- **Builds:** `deploy-wac-ota.sh`, `install-wac-device.sh` and `install-wac-simulator.sh` pass `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` for dev, staging and beta, and not for prod.
- **It needs a new SDK.** wac pins 0.7.169, which has no `RipulSiteSwitch`, so the branch builds only against an SDK release that has it. It was proved here with a local package override, which is not committed.

## The demo conversation: what the demo site would need

This is design only; none of it is applied.

### Why it fails today

The phone's side, `POST /v1/embedded-agents/<key>/session`, needs three things on the site it is pointed at. The demo has none of them:

1. **The wac app's sign-in on the site key:** `portalAuthOpaque` (`secret` and `secret-id` checked against WAC's `GET /api/v1/user`). The demo was cut off from every real system, so the key has none, and the handler answers 409 "This site needs a supported customer authentication provider".
2. **A CMS origin the sign-in validates against.** The handler fingerprints `config.originId` against the definition's origins. A wrapper inherits no origins, so the demo has none.
3. **`embeddedAgents` on the demo's definition.** Without it, `configured()` answers 404 "Authenticated agents are not enabled for this site".

   - It points at WAC's Rails base URL, the same host as the real portal's `origin_wac`.
   - It is used only by the opaque sign-in check, with no routes or pipelines bound to it, so no WAC data can be read through it.
   - **George needs to agree to this.** It is the one link from the demo to a real system. It reads only the signed-in phone user's own `/api/v1/user`, which proves who they are.
2. **The site key `sk_479undka5gp4`:**

   - `membershipPolicy: 'invite-only'`, so no one is enrolled automatically.
   - `allowedOrigins` containing `https://wac-ios.app`. Check this first; the switch's dropdown also hides the site without it.
3. **One test employee.** One row in the wrapper's own employees table (`employees_8fmfr6zq`): an invented person in company `DEMO`, status active, with a new code such as `DEM-PILOT01`, in the same columns as the real mapping (`unique_code`, `employee_code`, `company_id`, `status`).
4. **`embeddedAgents` on `cms_8fmfr6zq7mhn`**, through the wrapper's own setting (`wrapperHandlers.ts` accepts it):
   ```json

                  "statusColumn": "status", "displayNameColumn": "<as on wac>", "activeValues": ["active"], "formerValues": ["in-active"] }
   }
   ```
   - **Where the blanks come from:** copy each `<as on wac>` from the live `wac` mapping when this is applied.
   - **Why it is limited:** `allowedOrganisationIds` and `allowedBindingKeys` confine it to Demo Company and the one code, and the runner refuses everyone else.
5. **The phone:**
   - **The build:** a beta or dev wac build with the switch, from the embedded-agents branch merged with this one, pointed at "wac Demo" from the dev helper.
   - **Who signs in:** someone who belongs to the demo site. George's Ripul user does; Peter's is an admin.
   - **The account:** the wac account on the phone, a test account and never a client's employee, claims `DEM-PILOT01` in the Helper.
6. **The issue:** opened as on the real portal, with the operator `POST /admin/cms-definitions/cms_8fmfr6zq7mhn/embedded-agent-issues`.
   - It needs the claimed employment, an issue key and facts from one of that employee's invented shifts in `demo_shifts_8fmfr6zq`: rota against actual, with breaks.
   - George then joins the conversation from the to-do in the demo portal, signed in as `georgina+demo`.

**Unchanged:** data, company isolation and the copy (`wac-demo`). Nothing on `wac` or Inflato changes.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: mcp__ripul_tools__milestone
entries.description:
Record what this chat has achieved, as milestones: coarser than commits, and the list the user reads to see where a long chat has got to. Each one shows in the chat's side panel and jumps to its place in the conversation. Ripul attaches the time, the place in the chat, and the commits and deploys since the previous milestone. You supply words only.

Record one when the work reaches it, without being asked:
- The test: would you say it in one line if asked what this chat got done? A commit is not a milestone. Neither is a passing build.
- Reached means checked: seen working at the level the work calls for (live, on the device), not just committed.
- Two kinds: `delivered` (something now works or has shipped) and `decided` (a choice that later work rests on).
- Amend before adding: when the same outcome moves on ("on the simulator", then "on the phone"), pass that milestone's `id` with its new title.
- When the user asks for one, record it.

Call with `title` to record one, with `id` to amend one you wrote, with `goal` to say what the chat is working toward now, or with no arguments to list the chat's milestones. A milestone the user wrote or changed is theirs and is not amended. `atCommit` places a milestone in the past, at that commit, to catch up a chat that is already long.
To read other agents' milestones, use read_milestones.

atCommit.description: A commit sha. Places the new milestone at that commit's time. Only for catching up past work.

detail.description: One or two sentences, at most 300 characters. Optional.

goal.description: One line saying what the chat is working toward now. An empty string clears it.

id.description: The id of a milestone to amend, from this tool's list.

title.description: The outcome in one line of at most 80 characters, in words the user would use, e.g. "Sign-in works on the phone".

content.text:
The site switch is built on two pushed, unmerged branches, with nothing deployed, installed or changed on a live site. It can't be used yet: wac pins SDK 0.7.169, so its branch builds only after an SDK release that has the switch. And building wac against the current SDK `main` fails to link, for an unrelated reason in the SDK.

## Branches and commits (all named `sdk-site-key-switch`)
**ripul** (worktree `/tmp/ripul-site-key-switch`, from `main` at `3b634c66f`):
- `dd40e293b` server: the endpoint that lists a person's sites
- `427aa6706` SDK: the switch, the "Ripul Site…" menu row, the marker, reset on sign-out
- `2516694b8` SDK: the marker shows when a scene opens; 7 tests
- `fa9018e78` upload check refuses the switch; 6 tests
- `6da1ff36c`, `5ec710a08` plan: `chrome-extension/docs/plans/sdk-site-key-switch.md`

**wac iOS** (worktree `/tmp/wac-site-key-switch`, from `origin/v3` at `882ff569d`):
- `9c3a01fb7` Ripul site key and CMS id read through the switch, the build scripts, the TestFlight check and its tests

The shared checkouts were not touched. The ripul checkout already had 4 modified files from another agent, which I left alone.

## What existed vs what I built
- **The dev helper existed.** It is the SDK's `RipulDevAssistantOverlay` with its developer console; wac sets it up in `RipulDevConsoleConfig`, inside `#if WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.
- **It isn't really stripped from prod.** wac's TestFlight script refuses any configuration with `WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`, so only prod can be uploaded at all. But a prod `Release` build I made for the simulator still contains the SDK's helper code (`RipulDevAssistantOverlay`, `ConsoleLogViewer`, `RipulAgentConsole`). Only wac's own setup and the ways to open it are compiled out.
- **No endpoint listed a person's sites,** so I added one.
- **I built** the switch, the picker, the marker and reset, the endpoint, both upload checks and the wac wiring.

## The compile-time condition: `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` (new)
- **It turns on:** the switch is compiled in under `DEBUG || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD || RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`.
- **Why not `DEBUG`:** wac's beta is a Release configuration.
- **Why not `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`:** it brings in Live View's private-API touch code.
- **Why a command-line flag:** an app target's compile conditions don't reach the SDK package; only the xcodebuild command line does.
- **Who sets it:** wac's OTA, device and simulator scripts, for dev, staging and beta only. Never prod, never a project file.
- **A store build keeps only a pass-through:** `RipulSiteSwitch.siteKey(compiled:)` returns the key it is given.
- **Measured:** the SDK's release objects have no marker or endpoint string (50 KB). With the flag they have both (212 KB). In a wac beta build with the flag, the marker reaches the SDK object; in prod it doesn't.

## The server endpoint: `GET /v1/site-key/memberships?origin=…`
- **Who may call it:** only a person's own Ripul sign-in. A site key or machine token gets a 403.
- **Rows matched by user id only:** never by email, because a customer's own sign-in system could claim any email.
- **What it lists:** active memberships on enabled keys. With `origin`, only keys that accept the app's origin.
- **What it returns:** for each site, its key id, publishable key, name, slug, CMS id (following delegation) and role. Nothing is cached.
- **It grants nothing:** each site's own checks still decide every request.

## The upload checks
- **Ripul:** `check_private_apis.py` now treats `RIPUL_SITE_SWITCH_COMPILED_IN` as a never-allowed name, and `--allow-known` does not let it through.
- **wac, settings:** `deploy-testflight.sh` also refuses a configuration with `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_TOOLS` or `RIPUL_DEVELOPER_BUILD`.
- **wac, binary:** a new `check_store_build.py` reads the IPA before upload, in upload-only mode too.
  - It refuses the switch and wac's dev-helper setup.
  - It only reports the SDK's helper code, since every build carries that today; `WAC_STRICT_DEV_HELPER=1` makes it refuse.
- **On real builds:** the prod probe passes. The current beta build is refused, as it should be.

## Tests and builds
- **Server:** 5 new tests pass, and all 112 site-key and embedded-agent tests pass. The full `npx tsgo --noEmit` has 0 errors.
- **SDK:** `swift build` and the iOS simulator build pass, and so does a release build for the simulator with and without the flag. The 7 switch tests pass.
- **Checks:** 6 Python tests pass in each repo. The theme, sheet and private-API checks are clean, except one theme-lint warning I read as a false positive and left as it is (`SessionListMenu.swift:170`).
- **wac against the local SDK, prod and beta:** every source compiles, but **both fail at link**. SDK `main`'s `CmsVarianceImpactBlockView` uses Charts' `cornerRadius(_:style:)`, which is undefined when wac links. It needs fixing in the SDK before the next wac bump. I didn't fix it.
- **Not run:** nothing has run in an app or on a simulator yet.
- **Probe builds were deleted.** The SDK's `.build` folder inside my ripul worktree is still there; it is gitignored.

## Conversation design for the demo (design only, in the plan)
1. **An origin on the wrapper for sign-in only.** It points at WAC's Rails and checks only the signed-in phone user's own `/api/v1/user`, with no routes. It is the one link from the demo to a real system, so **George needs to agree to it.**
2. **The demo site key `sk_479undka5gp4`:**
   - the wac app's sign-in (`portalAuthOpaque`, copied from `sk_3b7wtby33l2n`);
   - invite-only membership;
   - `https://wac-ios.app` in its allowed origins (check this first: the picker also hides sites without it).
3. **One invented test employee** with a code such as `DEM-PILOT01` in `employees_8fmfr6zq`.
4. **The wrapper's embedded-agents setting:** allowed companies `["DEMO"]`, allowed codes `["DEM-PILOT01"]`, and `georgina+demo@wac.rocks` as Demo Company's manager.
5. **A test wac account on the phone** claims the code; then an issue is opened from one of that employee's invented demo shifts.

## Needs Peter's decision after the freeze
1. Merge ripul and run `deploy:all`, so the endpoint is live.
2. Fix the Charts link error, publish an SDK release, and bump wac's pinned version.
3. Merge the wac branch into `v3`, and with `feature/embedded-agent-reconciliation` for conversations.
4. Build a beta or dev OTA and install it on a test phone.
5. Make the demo site changes 1–4 above, once George has agreed.
6. Open the demo issue.

**Still open:**
- **Compiling the helper out of the SDK** for prod: not done.
- **Switching takes a quit and reopen:** screens already open keep the old site. The picker says so.
